utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Today is Tuesday, the 5th of September 2006. I'd like to say good afternoon to everyone here representatives of the Prosecution, of the Defence and the accused, as well as all the staff in this courtroom. We have to proceed with the direct examination of the witness who is here in the courtroom but before we proceed let me raise the following issue. Through a motion of the 1st of September, 2006, the Prosecution had applied to the Chamber for the admission of the exhibit submitted during the hearing of Manolic. A chart had been annexed to this application by the Prosecution, but we noticed that there was a mixture of exhibits that had been tendered and exhibits that had not been submitted, so we'd like to ask the Prosecution to submit a new application in which they will make a clear distinction between one type of exhibits and the other type of exhibits. And we'd like to invite the Defence, once they receive the application, to make any comments they have within the time prescribed, within the eight days that we indicated. I wanted to make that very clear in order for us to be able to rule very quickly on that matter. As a general rule, let me invite both the Prosecution and the Defence, when clarifications -- when you need clarification, please get in touch with the Trial Chamber's legal officer, who will be able to clarify a number of points for you. Of course, this does not prevent you from raising the issue during the hearing, but that's a good way, a practical way of resolving a number of issues. So I'd like to invite you to use the services of the Trial Chamber legal officer in order to solve a number of issues or to clarify a number of points. Having said that, I'm now going to give the floor to Mr. Scott to proceed with the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, if we could continue on, I'd like to ask you a series of questions continuing on with the procedures of how the HVO and its various departments conducted their work. And I'd ask that the witness please be shown Exhibit P 09530. If we could scroll down a bit maybe so the witness can -- thank you very much. Mr. Tomljanovich, can you first of all introduce this document to us, what it is, and how it relates to the work that you did.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the Rules of Procedure of the HVO HZ HB, and they're signed, if we could look at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, it would be the bottom of the last page.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bottom of the last page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And for reference, I believe it's page 8. It would be page 18. Maybe the numbering is off. It may be page 16 in e-court, I'm not sure?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Signed by Jadranko Prlic on the 14th of October, 1992, and this outlines the procedure by which the HVO HZ HB or the cabinet of the HVO undertook its business. This seems to be for the most part a confirming would be the practice which you find in the minutes of the meetings which preceded as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go back to the second page of the document starting with Article 2 or if -- perhaps we can look at the top of that -- I'm sorry, if we can look at the top of that page. It says: "These rules of procedure shall regulate the work of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna hereinafter the HVO." If I could first direct your attention to Article 4: "The HVO shall programme its work to ensure its higher performance." Did you see documentation and records, Mr. Tomljanovich, that indicated that that practice was generally followed?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was followed. First of all, I should explain that when they say they shall programme its work or say that the work shall be programmatic, that means that each department has to come up with a plan for its activity in the near future which has to be implemented and the implementation of each department's plan is supposed to be overseen by the president and the secretary of the HVO HZ HB. And finally -- yes, in fact, I have seen such programmes or plans and one is cited in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Going over to Article 8 on the following page, please. Is what is said in Article 8 in fact consistent with what you just described to us a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That the programme of work is adopted by the HVO and then that the president and secretary of the HVO supervise the implementation of the general HVO programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does the document then go on to actually regulate the way that the sessions, the meetings of the HVO HZ HB themselves are actually conducted?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This document contains what are the rules of order for meetings of the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if we go over to -- starting at Article 10, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At Article 10 the president and secretary are charged with supervising the organisation and preparation of the sessions. And the articles that follow, follow the procedure which I outlined yesterday. The agendas would be circulated to all the members along with any documentation they needed to read prior to the meeting, which usually included proposed legislation, and then the meeting was held and would follow that agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I think just one final item before we move forward. If you'll look at Article 34, which I believe would be on approximately page 11 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Article 34 simply reads that the decrees and decisions that are passed at these meetings shall be published in the Narodni List HZ HB and the dispositions and conclusions will only be published when it's so decided by the HVO. And I could add that on occasion they did not publish certain dispositions and conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think we saw one or more of these yesterday, but can you tell the Judges again if, either way, did the HVO and its departments have the practice of providing semi-annual reports on its work and activities for the preceding six-month period?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and the general HVO semi-annual reports are compilations of those departmental reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could direct our attention briefly to Exhibit P 04699. Can you tell the Judges what that document is, sir.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second semi-annual report of the HVO HZ HB finally approved on September of 1993, but it covers the activity of the first half of 1993. And it also states that it was formally adopted and approved at the 49th meeting of the HVO HZ HB on the 7th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask to go to, just to pick out a couple of examples of how these reports work, to page 16 of the document, please. And toward the bottom half of the page. Thank you. Do you see a paragraph there, sir, about -- the paragraph starting with the language "In the period, over six thousand prisoners of war stayed in appropriate centres on the territory"?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does that paragraph go on to indicate: "Prison governors have been appointed to undertake all coordination work. The military police have the task of providing security for prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It also mentions that the detainees are interrogated by SIS officers, and I should explain to the Judges: The SIS was military counter-intelligence. And also by crime investigation services the governors have been appointed and the military police have the task for providing for security. And they also mention that there's the problem of forced entry and violent investigation which has been registered by some commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Has it been registered by some commanders or is it, rather, the violent investigation that was done by some or attributed to some commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a good question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should look at the -- I should look at the B/C/S original. I assume that it was -- the commanders were registering the behaviour, but if I could look -- do we have the B/C/S copy there? That might make it clearer, although it might not be any clearer in the original as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have the original?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I have the binder of semi-annual reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have it. With the usher's assistance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we know what the corresponding B/C/S page is?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't have it, Mr. Tomljanovich, in my notes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. There we are. Looking at the -- hmm. I'm not sure it's necessarily any clearer in the Croatian. I'll read it out in the original. The sentence reads: [Interpretation] "Forceful entry and forceful carrying out of investigations by certain commanders was noted." [In English] Yeah, this translation, it would say "by certain commanders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: This would -- this would go along with the next sentence which says that the behaviour should definitely be prohibited and prevented.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Do you know whether any follow-up occurred? Do you know what -- what was done to prohibit and prevent? And prevention is more important in such behaviour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there are a number of documents I cite in my report dealing with the situation in the camps and various discussion of similar problems by various HVO functionaries. I think we probably will be getting to those later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If we could then -- we have looked at -- sorry, I'm just looking for what we covered yesterday. I believe we may have looked at -- yesterday at Exhibit P 04735. Really, mostly a procedural question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting, but there's a misunderstanding here, and I'd like to deal with that. This Javier report has two numbers, and the witness's report has them as two different exhibits. So the number is 04699. Can we check those numbers? And then we have -- that's the exhibit. And then after that we have another exhibit. Just let me find the number. 4735, which is in fact a continuation of that report, if I'm right. Do I understand that correctly? Because they're different numbers, so one gains the impression that the Prosecutor is referring to two different reports, whereas it's a continuation of the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exactly the next point in my outline, Counsel. Yes, for whatever reason when the documents were originally prepared the report was -- somehow became divided in two, and so counsel is right and that's about -- again what I was about to explain. P 04699 is the first half of the report for the first six months of 1993, and P 04735 is the second half of that same report, again covering the first six months of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you'd like, Mr. Tomljanovich, just to confirm that. If you could -- and we can probably do it just by looking at the electronic version, to save time, perhaps. If we could pull up P 04735.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly the case. It was -- initially when the two documents were scanned in the second and third semi-annual reports, the end of the second report was scanned in with the third report mistakenly. So we've split up the second report under the two -- or the second report then was split into two halves but it should be -- the original document was these two exhibits. It was a problem with the scanning in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can just look at -- yes. All right. Can you look on the screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just confirm for the Judges, is that document the second half?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to look further up. I only see a paragraph in the middle. Let me see, here, in my original. It should be. It starts right in the middle. It's -- I forget which page it is in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps I'm belabouring it too much with that explanation. Perhaps that's sufficient but -- yes, indeed it is part of the same document.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although I can't find it in my copy here, that particular section, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's go forward, then, sir, if we can. I'd like to direct your attention to a series of events in January of 1993. The Judges have already received significant amount of -- a significant amount of evidence on various international negotiations that were taking place in early 1993, in particular concerning the Vance-Owen Plan. Can -- and in this context, in fact, there have been references to what has been called a "ultimatum" issued by the HVO on the 15th of January, 1993. Can you assist the Judges, Mr. Tomljanovich, by putting this in the context of the HVO structures, processes and orders that you saw connected with that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I do see in the report, and I begin with discussing the order which was issued by Mr. Prlic on the 15th of January, 1993. Now, the reason this is called an ultimatum is because this order says that troops in the Vance-Owen provinces 3, 8, and 10, should either submit to HVO control or leave the territory. Conversely, HVO troops in other provinces should submit to ABiH control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we have, please, Exhibit P 01146. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is that a copy of the decision of the 15th of April, 1993 -- excuse me, January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see the translation of one of the copies of this document. We found quite a few copies of this particular document in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may make a point of clarification. The gentleman indicated that there was an order. There is a vast difference between an order and a decision. I would appreciate if such terminology is used with precision and accuracy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can look and direct your attention to paragraph number 1 of the decision, and scroll down the page, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I said earlier, that all units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina which at this moment are stationed in provinces 3, 8, and 10. Now, these are the provinces, the proposed provinces of the Vance-Owen Plan which would have had Croatian majorities. And then it goes on to say here, "... which have been declared Croatian provinces in the Geneva Accords shall be subordinated to the Main Staff of the HVO armed forces." And the converse is true when you see in section -- or paragraph number 2, the converse is true in provinces 1, 5, and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you go over to the second page of the document, please, and direct your attention to Article 5, and --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that it was called an ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does this document give a deadline?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it does. It sets it at five days from the 15th of January, which would be presumably the 20th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the decision was issued over the name or the signature of --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Jadranko Prlic. And in the preamble it says that this decision was reached at an extraordinary session of the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does article -- or, excuse me, paragraph 6 indicate who should implement this order?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, this decision.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, and it should be implemented by the head of the defence department of the HVO HZ HB, which at this time would have been Mr. Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we then it please go to Exhibit P 01140, P 01140. Before that -- well, it's probably too late. Go ahead. It's all right. Can you tell us what that document is, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the order of Mr. Stojic which follows on the document from Mr. Prlic earlier stating exactly how the previous decision is to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he's passing it on down the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in the opening paragraph, if you look at the very introductory paragraph --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- above the word "order," do you see a reference to a decision?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he makes a reference to the decision HVO HZ HB number 01-I-32/93, the 15th of January, 1993, which is the exhibit we just looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Looking at paragraph number 7 of this order, does it again indicate a deadline?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It's worded slightly different here. Mr. Stojic says explicitly the 20th of January rather than saying five days after the is 15th of January, and he gives a specific time and that's 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you explain to us what paragraph 8 indicates?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see half of it. "Chief of the Main Staff and the armed forces of the HVO and the --" if I could see the next page. Yes. "And the chief of the HVO military police administration shall be responsible to me," me in this case being Mr. Stojic, "for implementation of this order." So he's passing it another step down the line to the chief of staff and to the head of the military police which at this time would have been Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in fact then if we could next go to Exhibit P 01156, and can you tell us what that is, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe since the HVO main headquarters -- I believe this is Mr. Petkovic's order, although, could I see the bottom quickly?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The next page.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe this is Mr. Petkovic's order. Yes, it is. Further transferring the same order down to the operational zones or the operative zones of Southeastern Herzegovina, Northwestern Herzegovina and Central Bosnia as well as the 1st Mostar Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go back, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just going to mention --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can go back to the first page, please, so the Judges can see that particular language. Paragraphs 1 and 2 or the introductory paragraph, I should say, and 1. Thank you. The reference orders -- it says, "pursuant to the decision of." Do those reference documents relate to, first of all, the first one being the decision of Mr. Prlic and the second one being the order of Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go ahead. I'm sorry, you wanted to say something --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. All I was going to say was that he sends it to every operational zone with the exception of the Posavina Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I add a question on this document? Is point 4 here something which is different from the two parent decisions and order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe, and I'd have to be 100 per cent sure I'd have to look at Mr. Stojic's order again to be sure it's not in there, but I do believe this is the first time that's stated explicitly, that these units would be treated as paramilitary units and disarmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say with certainty that was not the language in Mr. Prlic's original order. I'm sorry, decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can assist. If I could -- if we can go back to then Mr. Stojic's order of P 01140, and specifically to paragraph number 3.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you to look at the end of that sentence and see if there's something similar to --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm sorry I'd forgotten that there was similar language in the order of Mr. Stojic. It does say that any of these units which do not subordinate themselves to the relevant command will be treated as members of paramilitary units and disarmed. That was an oversight on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: And taken into custody, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Continuing with this series of events can I ask you next to be shown P 01184. And can you tell us what that is and --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes this --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- and the purpose of including that in are report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a letter by Jadranko Prlic to the Croatian people of Gornji Vakuf, to the HVO of Gornji Vakuf which is the municipal government of Gornji Vakuf and to the HVO command which would be the municipal military headquarters discussing the events in the aftermath of the issuance of this ultimatum and giving full support to the Croats in Gornji Vakuf where there'd been fighting in the aftermath of this particular ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does it make reference to the fact that this communication was sent in connection with a session of the HVO HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well -- could we scroll down, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Or up --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- in paragraph ...

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It mentions that "at today's session," which the date, please, at the top. Or is it at the bottom? Unfortunately, I don't have a hard copy of this document. In any event, we'll scroll up to the top again, please. Thank you. That at the -- that day's session of the HVO HZ HB they discussed political and security conditions in the area of the HZ HB and particularly in the area of your municipality, which in this case is Gornji Vakuf municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In terms of a date reference, sir, if we can go back to the second page of the document. You might see there's a box on that page and I can just ask you --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- are you familiar with that kind of a stamp? Have you seen that on ^but the translation is a ^check ^15 translation of the receipt stamp from the HVO Main Staff. Generally speaking, the offices in various parts of the HVO are -- of the HZ HB armed forces and government would -- especially the military offices would stamp documents as received and give the time. And usually give serial numbers for the receipt as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this document was received on the 18th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in fact could we then go on to Exhibit P 01227.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- that's -- it's not on the e-court screen yet. But I have the hard copy here. I'll start discussing it. This is a meeting or minutes of a meeting of an extraordinary session of the HVO HZ HB. As I mentioned yesterday, the HVO HZ HB had its regular weekly sessions which were numbered and when they had pressing business they had extraordinary sessions, and this one, there's only one item on the agenda and that's the current situation in the HZ HB with -- in regards to or in view of the HZ HB -- HZ HB HVO decision of the 15th of January, 1993. And importantly -- the most important thing here is the first full paragraph which states: "Analysing the implementation of the HZ HB HVO decision of 15 January 1993 the head of the HZ HB HVO defence department, Mr. B. Stojic, among other things, lists the situation in Gornji Vakuf as calming down after attacks of extremist Muslim forces and ABiH," that's army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, "units on settlements within that municipality, inhabited by Croats, and attacks on Croatian Defence Council units have been stopped." Now, the significance of this passage is that this fighting in Gornji Vakuf is being linked directly to the decision of the -- as part of the implement -- linked -- as part of the implementation of the decision of the 15th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Looking up you have mentioned that this -- these statement of this report is attributed to Mr. Stojic. If we go up into the introductory part of the document and indicating those present --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- do you see Mr. Stojic listed as one of the persons present?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is. He's the third person listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us from your review of these minutes of HVO HZ HB meetings, were they typically attended not only by Mr. Prlic but by Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of all the available meetings we have, Mr. Prlic is at all of them. Mr. Stojic is not at all of them, but if he does not attend his deputy head of the department attends in his place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of his deputy?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may interject here, a point of clarification, Your Honour. As you well know we've heard testimony thus far that there had been fighting in Gornji Vakuf the days preceding the 15th. Are we to assume that this gentleman is stating here today under oath that there was no fighting in Gornji Vakuf prior to the 15th and this is the only interpretation that can be given to this particular decision? I think we need a point of clarification in light of the testimony that we've had before this Tribunal thus far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that's an accurate characterisation of what Mr. Tomljanovich said. He simply said there was a linkage between the events in Gornji Vakuf and implementation of this decision. There is no indication that that was the only fighting or when the fighting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The implication, Your Honour, is, and if we look at the indictment there's -- the Prosecution is making a linkage, that as a result of the decision of the 15th, you had this heavy fighting going on in Gornji Vakuf. Our -- our position has been and will remain that there were -- the Gornji Vakuf incident or incidents had occurred much earlier and as a result of trying to put an end to these situations, the decision based on what was happening in Geneva was issued. So I think this is major point that needs clarification, and this man is a historian. So I would assume that as a historian with a Ph.D., he would appreciate and understand the significance of these events as opposed to merely making some sort of a conclusory remark. That's why I think at this point in time a point of clarification may be needed. I can go into it on my cross-examination, but I think now is the time, because I think if he's going to be putting things into context in talking about background, now is the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise once again for interrupting, but following on from what my learned friend has just said, it would be a very good idea if the witness were to read out the second sentence just to link up this ultimatum with the exhibit. I know that I can do that during the cross-examination, of course, but I think that it would be very important for the witness to read out the second sentence since we have this exhibit and the conclusion that the witness drew on reading just the first sentence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to try and speed up. Let's hear the second sentence read out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second sentence, it's the next paragraph states that, "HVO armed forces which were under explicit orders not to engage in any combat activity were successful in preventing an enemy offensive, and at the same time creating panic among the enemy. This resulted in a large number of extremists surrendering to the HVO forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can be shown please Exhibit P 01305.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would really be interested in the witness telling us what happened preceding the 15th of January in Gornji Vakuf. This second sentence is not very clear. How does one prevent an offensive by not engaging in -- in combat? I would like to know what do we have to -- to imagine what -- what is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't answer that question either. I don't know what the military situation in Gornji Vakuf was exactly. That goes beyond the scope of my report, so I can't make any comment on that. Nor can I comment on what was going on either before this report or before the 15th of January necessarily, other than what I've seen in the documents I looked at, which are looking at it from the level of Mostar and a national level. But specifically what's going on locally, I'm sorry, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I might assist. If I can remind the Chamber that of course there will be other fact witnesses that will be addressing all of these matters, other international monitors, victim witnesses who will talk extensively about what happened in Gornji Vakuf during this time. If I could ask you please to go to Exhibit P 01305. Can you he will it us sir what that is and how it relates to the part of your report dealing with the sequence of documents relating to the events in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a letter from Mr. Prlic to the then Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia Hrvoje Sarinic on the 25th of January, 1993, appealing for his assistance in the wake of these events following the 15th of January, following the 20th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the text of Mr. Prlic's letter, can you -- you may need the assistance of the usher in leafing or going on to the other pages?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does he request that specific actions being taken by the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He does as a matter of fact and I'll check very quickly again to see if I have this exhibit already in hard copy. Which -- 1, 3 -- no, unfortunately I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If we can -- if the usher can go forward to page 3 of the document, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can look at that, sir, and just give us an overview.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep. He's requesting aid from the Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia, and the number -- the specific measures that Mr. Prlic recommends is informing international officials of the situation which he describes above, requesting from Mr. Alija Izetbegovic to end the operations carried out by forces under his jurisdiction, and the third point is to suspend all forms of aid being shipped from or through the territory of the Republic of Croatia, particularly the supply of weapons and equipment and materiel for military purposes. I presume this discusses the military aid being sent to the ABiH although that's not explicitly stated. Next point is to explain to humanitarian organisations why due to military operations and roads they've prohibited transport along the humanitarian corridors and then finally to influence the media in the Republic of Croatia in regards to the events described above. And here I could add from some of the other meetings and some of the other documents which I cite in my report the leadership of the HVO HZ HB was upset about some of the press coverage they'd been getting in the Republic of Croatia, particularly from the newspaper Slobodna Dalmacija from Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges in looking at the --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, you --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was just going to say -- I'm sorry. Could we scroll down just a tiny bit? Because the final thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to come back to what you had just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- insinuated. Can you give us more specific information about what I understand to have been a negative press in the newspaper you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the specific item, and I believe this is cited specifically in my report and that I cite this, they were upset how Slobodna Dalmacija had been covering the events in Gornji Vakuf. I forget the specific wording but I think they were upset that the number of civilian casualties which the newspaper, which was a daily paper, Slobodna Dalmacija, was claiming had occurred in Gornji Vakuf at that time. And I believe that's in one of the cabinet meetings from right around this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And was the allegation that the HVO caused these -- these civilian deaths?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure because I didn't go and check Slobodna Dalmacija for those days, but clearly they were portrayed in a negative light in relation to those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the questioning, first of all, I would request that the gentleman cite exactly where in his report; secondly, just on this last admission, it appears that he hasn't even read the articles of which he's quoting, an and now we're getting into a slippery slope. Also, I just wish to point out and I didn't want to do so even at the urgings of my co-counsel, that when he read the paragraph true information to carry out true information somehow he omitted to point that out. Now, you know, I'm going to try to calm down during these proceedings, but it's these sort of things that I see that are rather, in my opinion, inconsistent with trying to get the truth out to this Trial Chamber, because obviously there is a problem here. In carrying out true information. I think this is very relevant, you know. So -- and if there are articles, let him produce them. But obviously Mr. Prlic at least in this instance is saying, Look, get out the true information whatever that information may be. Transparency. Obviously they have nothing to hide. It goes to any motives or --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I guess Mr. Karnavas is testifying now on behalf of his client, Your Honours. This is -- this is colour commentary we've come across before. There's no place for it at all. Counsel can state his objection according to the Rules of Evidence and Procedure, and the commentary and argument and attacks on the witness or counsel are not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's not an attack. It's clear -- I'm pointing out a fact. The gentleman -- it's on the screen. It's in the record. I'm not attacking. This is where I think I feel like I'm being victimised here, because I think when a witness intentionally and purposely who works for the Prosecution omits critical words --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There he goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- I think they need to be pointed out on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Karnavas, the question that you've just raised is an interesting one and a relevant one, but you could have raised it during the cross-examination, because proceeding in this way you are making it impossible for the Prosecution to conduct its business. You're taking up time. So you'll have every opportunity to come back to the question, but I have a much more important question that I'd like to ask the witness and raise with the witness. This document, I note that it is a letter of the 25th of January written at 2200 hours, that is to say 10.00 p.m. So a priori, the person signing the letter, Mr. Prlic, attaches great importance to the contents of the letter that is addressed to Mr. Sarinic, who is the Prime Minister. Now, in the work -- in your work as an expert and historian, did you see if there was an answer to the letter, a response by the Croatian Prime Minister? Because in this particular letter, it is suggested to the Croatian Prime Minister to take action on several levels. First of all, to inform the international community of what is going on, to ask Mr. Izetbegovic to intervene, and to temporarily suspend all circulation of arms, ammunition, and others, and to explain to the humanitarian organisations, international ones, the consequences of that offensive. Now, was there a response, an answer to that letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, if there was a response I've never seen it and as far as I know we don't have that document in our possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes. I thought that might be the question -- the answer, because otherwise this would have been annexed to the first letter. But I just wanted to clear that up. Please proceed, Mr. Scott. And we'll come back to the questions raised by Mr. Karnavas during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could then go to Exhibit P 01317.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, could I finish the answer I was giving you earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just -- let me caution you, Mr. Tomljanovich. I mean, I know some we all get in a hurry and try to save time.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you're going to read directly from the document, go ahead and take the time to read it verbatim.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I apologise for that. I was intending to paraphrase. If I could go back to the end of this document where we were just second -- oh, I'm sorry. We've already moved on to the next document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, if you still have the -- if you have the earlier document in front of you, go ahead and make the comment you want to make.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I was just going to make the comment that the last thing Mr. Prlic says is that, if -- and I'm paraphrasing since I don't have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we all go back then to the last document, P 01305 to avoid any controversy about what was said. The bottom of the last -- the bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next page, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sorry, bottom of the third page.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I was going to read the last part here which now -- this is a quote. "If we assess that the situation is growing more complex and thus become unmanageable within scope of our capabilities we shall have no choice but to ask for military assistance from the Republic of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall during what period of time Mr. Sarinic was in the position of Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Much of 1992, certainly the last half of 1992, until some point shortly after this when he was replaced by Mr. Nikica Valentic. It would have been late -- late winter or early fall of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go back to --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, late winter or other spring, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go forward to Exhibit P 01317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. The witness raised the weight of the last paragraph. You've just read out the paragraph which seems to say that Mr. Prlic was telling the Prime Minister of Croatia that unless the situation improved he was going to ask for military assistance from Croatia. Now, as an expert and historian yourself, did you study the documents in your possession -- in your possession provided by the Prosecution and undertake historical research to see whether before that date, that is to say the 25th of January, Croatia already did provide military assistance or whether it was as of this particular date that it was going to send military assistance? Did you ask yourself that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, absolutely. Not just for this report but this is an issue which has come up in all of the trials we've had involving the HVO and Herceg-Bosna. And certainly there was military assistance prior to this date. There was assistance in training and assistance with materials, and certainly at least in the border areas, and no one contests this, there was the presence of Croatian troops, although as far as I know prior to January of 1993 there were no actual Croatian HV, Croatian army troops in Bosnia and Herzegovina outside of a couple of the border areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how the Croatian was translated into English, but when I see the English sentence it says, "We shall have no choice but to ask for military assistance." That means that, if one is precise, they should have asked to continue assistance, whereas here we gain the impression that this is asking for assistance and not for the continuation of assistance. So how do you explain that? How do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well -- now, once again I'm speculating and I'm not saying this on the basis of anything explicit in any documents I've seen; however, there are two reasons for that, I suspect. One, I suspect what Mr. Prlic means here is not that they will request military assistance in terms of more material but that they will request military assistance in terms of direct intervention or the sending of HV troops which did indeed happen later. Now, the other thing which has to be kept in mind is that all throughout this period and even after the war the legal fiction was maintained that Croatia -- the Republic of Croatia was not militarily involved in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So that may be another explanation, although once again I can't say that based on anything I've seen explicitly from any document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm sure we'll have an opportunity to come back to that. Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could then go forward to P 01317. Can you tell us what that is, please, and also if it bears any connection to the letter to Prime Minister Sarinic?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- these are the conclusions of an emergency meeting of the HVO HZ HB held on the 26th of January, 1993, and this document is issued under the serial numbers of Mr. Prlic, and these conclusions relate to the fighting in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at the items in the -- most of the body of the report, do you see any similarity between this and the letter sent to the Croatian Prime Minister?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a -- the situation is being described in similar terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, just so there's no confusion, when you -- this is a report of the session on the 26th of January, 1993. Directing your attention to the paragraph on the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have any information that any of the statements being made here by Mr. Prlic are in fact true?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do know that there was an incident in Dusina at this time committed by ABiH forces, but as far as the specifics are concerned, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Prlic indicates here "There is still no accurate information about casualties"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. "... but it's known that 33 HVO soldiers were killed," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've been reminded again to tender the exhibits as we go, and to catch up with where we are, I will now tender P 09530 -- yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before you do, one follow-up question related to this last document. Let me move to point 7. It is stated that the government of the Republic of Croatia was informed of a situation. Their assistance was requested depending on the turn of event. Here there's nothing about military assistance. Between the letter we saw previously and that meeting that took place on the next day, did you see an evolution, a difference? Why isn't the military factor clearly mentioned? Have you wondered about it? Have you asked yourself that question? Because that's a question I immediately ask myself when I read these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not necessarily, because there's a few explanations for that. One is that there was an evolution in the position. The other is just that it wasn't formulated very specifically in this next document. And having no other information to go on, I really don't know which or if something else is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Scott, your numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. P 09530, P 04699, P 04735, P 01146, P 01140, P 01156, P 01184, P 01227, P 01305, and P 01317. The reason I hesitated, Your Honour, is because I -- because obviously we are listing these in the order in which they're -- they came up in examination but not in numerical order. Obviously they're out of numerical order, but that's the order in which they've been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go forward, if we can, from January of 1993 to another situation, a series of documents in April of 1993. Can you tell the Judges, just to set the context, were there continuing developments concerning the Vance-Owen Plan by the latter part of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And briefly, what was the status of the Vance-Owen negotiations as of late March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it had been signed as well by both the Croatian and Muslim sides but that the maps had not been signed and some of the specifics had not yet been signed, but that it had not yet been approved by the Bosnian Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did your report indicate -- your research indicate that there was extensive discussion of these developments among the HVO records during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, particularly -- not so much in March but, yes, very much so in early April, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you to please direct your attention to P 01778.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What is that, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at a different document from what I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It should be 1778.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I was looking at 1778. I'm sorry. I don't have a hard copy, but this is the 33rd session of the HVO HZ HB held on the 1st of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just for these purposes, if I can direct your attention to the last page on page 7, item D -- item 8, subitem (d).

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yeah. This is the end of the meeting, and the last thing that's stated is that "the Vance-Owen Peace Plan documents must be provided so that it can be discussed at the regular HVO HZ HB session on Saturday, 3rd of April, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you find, sir, in your inquiry that in fact those matters were discussed at the regular meeting on the 3rd of April?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you then to go to P 01798.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the minutes of that meeting that was held on the 3rd of April, 1993, and the agenda is one item, and that one item is the discussion of the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. And I'll say at the outset, the most unusual thing about this meeting is this is the only meeting which we have in our possession or only minutes of any meeting we have in our possession at which Mate Boban was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The only meeting of the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The only meeting of the HVO HZ HB that he was present for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell from this document whether despite the fact that Mr. Boban was there, did -- well, let me put it this way: If Mr. Boban was there, did he or did Mr. Prlic chair the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states there, "Present, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, who is chairing the meeting ..." So Mr. Prlic chaired the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, this document goes on for some time about these matters and I would just like for you, if you can, to take us through the document --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- And how it relates to the matters we were talking about this afternoon and the work done on your report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this meeting all of the participants discuss going forward or not going forward -- thank you -- discuss whether they should go forward or not go forward a -- with the idea of the ultimatum of 15th of January, 1993, and to subordinate ABiH units to the HVO in provinces 3, 8, and 10, on conversely -- or subordinate the ABi -- or the HVO units to the ABiH or the Muslim or what they consider to be the Muslim-proposed provinces. At the very beginning under item 1, it states, and I'm just paraphrasing the first couple of paragraphs. Mr. Mate Boban gives a report on the peace plan. It's described by him as being optimal. And in the second paragraph on page 2, I'll read that out entirely, second paragraph on page 2 after discussing the plan itself, Mr. Boban states: "The HVO HZ HB is also of the opinion that in all its important segments, the provisional system of executive government that has been established in the area --"

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Slow down a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... that has been established in this area --" or, sorry, "in the area of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, is entirely consistent with the powers of the provincial organs of government defined in the basic document and in the agreement on provisional organisation and that the system will be consistently applied in provinces 3," and there's a question mark next to 3 because the legibility, "8, and 10." Now, this states that the intention is that the system of government continue in these provinces such as it had been in the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I direct your attention to not the very next paragraph which is the --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- quote but the paragraph that begins the words "Until the republic is fully demilitarised."

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There is a reference in that paragraph to the joint statement of Mr. Mate Boban --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic. Can you tell us what that is a reference to?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a reference to the agreement or the alleged agreement under the six points on the next page, the substance of which is to subordinate to carry out the same -- to carry out the decision basically of the 15th of January, 1993, and put the army of BiH in provinces 3, 8, and 10 under the control of the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, before we -- I'm not going to take you through the six terms. Everyone will have that in front of them, but can you tell the Judges, please, was there in fact at this time -- was there in fact a joint statement signed by Boban and Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge there was not. And furthermore, if you look at the paragraph after the six points, the one which begins, and I'll read the full quote out here: "The HVO HZ HB hopes that because of the enormous importance of the Statement, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic will sign this document, because it is yet further evidence of a desire for peace, which everybody wants." So that one indicate that it had not yet been signed by Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does the discussion at this meeting go on to indicate what would happen if President Izetbegovic did not sign the joint statement?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And immediately in the next paragraph it says: "At this meeting the HVO HZ HB adopted the position that if the aforementioned Statement is not signed by the leaders of the Muslim delegations in provinces number 3, 8, and 10, then the basic premise in the Peace Plan, that all ethnic armed forces will have to withdraw to their domicile provinces, should apply." Next paragraph: "If the Joint Statement is not implemented, the appropriate military and other authorities of the HVO HZ HB shall implement this provision of the Basic Document of the peace plan in regions numbers 3, 8, and 10. At the same time, the HVO HZ HB will respect the jurisdiction of the authorities in the provinces predominantly populated by the two other peoples."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, I'm not going to ask you to quote it unless you feel the need to.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does the discussion indicate what would happen to various organs or institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina inside these provinces 3, 8, and 10 after this statement was enforced?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, and basically the same principle follows that followed for the military, for the police as well, and what they call "The police organs of the former Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina will cease to exist with the coming into force of the already-signed documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, and the public at large will be informed about the complete takeover of all powers by the Department of the Interior of the HVO HZ HB in provinces numbers 3, 8, and 10."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, during this meeting was there discussion of sending out various members or representatives of this body, the HVO HZ HB, around Herceg-Bosna to essentially, if you will, and my paraphrase, to get the word out?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. At the beginning of page 5 in the English translation, that's exactly what that one short paragraph says, that the members of the HVO HZ HB will visit municipalities and explain to the authorities the essence of the Vance-Owen documents and the conclusions of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And before we finish on this document, there are particular conclusions that are numbered there. Can you go to item number 9, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On the last page of --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Item number 9, which is the final conclusion, reads: "After the meeting, members of the HVO HZ HB will tour the front line."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you see any evidence in the documentation or the information that you had available to you that that in fact happened, that there were -- in fact representatives did go out around this time and that members of the HVO HZ HB did tour the front line?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the documentation I reviewed for the preparation of this report. I didn't see anything regarding members of the HVO HZ HB touring municipalities or the front line. However, I did see documentation regarding military personnel touring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to go next to Exhibit P 01788, unless there are questions. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just to be precise. Number 9 concerns visiting the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Now, you have told us that there is information on militaries visiting the municipalities --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- which would be something clearly different, wouldn't it? It's not the same thing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's entirely different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to put a question to you about this meeting that lasted four hours, the 34th session of the HVO with Mr. Boban, and they discussed the issue of a Vance-Owen Plan. As part of your work as an expert, did you compare the Vance-Owen Plan, on the one hand, with its many components, did you compare that with the points, with the items discussed during that meeting, and was there a coincidence, a total coincidence between what was discussed during that meeting and the very essence of the Vance-Owen Plan, or did you notice differences between the two, and if you noticed differences, what were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I -- I should state at the outset that I didn't review the peace plans themselves or the diplomatic situation for the writing of this report. This report was intended to deal with the governing structures and processes of Herceg-Bosna. However, I am familiar with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan and the primary difference between what's in this meeting or the view of the peace plan which is in this meeting and what I generally understood to be the essence of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, as I understand it from my earlier work here at the Tribunal, was that it was not the intention of the international community to cede these provinces to one particular ethnic group, rather, that the country would be divided into cantons in which certain ethnic groups would be majorities and many of them, which is a significant difference. The second difference from the reading of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan and from my understanding of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan just based on my knowledge, not on any work that I did for this report, is that the other sides did not intend for the plan to be immediately implemented before all parts of it had been approved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, these are the two main items you'd like to outline. First of all, according to the Vance-Owen Plan, there were supposed to be cantons with ethnic majorities that would vary from canton to canton, and the second main point was that the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan had not been defined extremely precisely, whereas in this, during that meeting, they already set a date for the implementation of the plan. I'm just trying to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- summarise what you've told us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And I should add, too, and this is probably a better way to put it, that I don't think the internationals or the other side realised that the implementation of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan would mean the extension of Herceg-Bosna authorities over provinces 3, 8 and 10 immediately and over all of those territories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think we'll have the opportunity to discuss that again during the cross-examination. We have five minutes left, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In this respect, then, in terms of the discussion of getting the people either going into the field, either to the front line or to municipalities, can I ask you please to look next at P 01788.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did your review of the documentation indicate that in fact on the day before the meeting Mr. Praljak and Mr. Coric had already travelled to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is what I was referring to when I mentioned military personnel visiting the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what does document -- or Exhibit P 01788 indicate?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should state at the beginning that this -- what we have in our hands, the one translation, isn't actually the whole document. This is an excerpt from a logbook from the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia, and it's in regards to a meeting which they held with General Praljak; he's referred to here as Colonel Dario Kordic; Mr. Ignac Kostroman, who was an HDZ official; Mr. Valentin Coric; as well as the commander of this particular Operational Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. And it's discussing this implementation of Vance-Owen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And does it indicate who chaired this particular part of the meeting and how long this part of the meeting lasted?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The meeting was chaired by General Praljak, and the meeting began at 10.30 in the morning, ended at noon. So it was an hour and a half long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give us, then, an overview, you can take us to any particular part of the document you wish, the discussion of this meeting as it relates to the Vance-Owen peace process, or the HVO view of that process?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Praljak begins the meeting, and I'll just point out a few sections of what he says that are of particular importance for that. In the first paragraph where he speaks, midway through the paragraph he states that: "This declaration establishes the immutability of the borders of the Republic of Croatia." Now, in parentheses there is a question mark because this isn't horribly legible. And the quote continues: "No way to change them anymore, peaceably or by force. The Republic of Croatia can now itself sign treaties with international organisations. This declaration represents a great victory and we must have patience." Now, the next paragraph, Mr. Praljak says that Mr. Izetbegovic's option for Bosnia-Herzegovina is finally out of the question. "He has signed." Further down in that same paragraph, he states: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna will remain. It will have its own Assembly, and the provincial government will rule the country." "The central government will have nothing." He continues. At the end of that section he says: "The West is not interested in history but in the number of Croats in these parts." And at the beginning of the next page of the translation, Praljak continues and says: "Salvation lies in protecting the population and enhancing the birth rate." Further down, he continues and says: "There will be moving out and resettlement, and the population will homogenise." Now, moving further down to the end of this page, a Mr. Borivoj Malbasic asked about Vares, and General Praljak said: "There is no policy that can capable us to have everything. If you think there is, tell us."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time, and we'll come back to this document after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 10 to 4.00. We'll resume at 10 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Mr. Scott, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, I think before the break you were addressing some comments towards the bottom of page 2 of the report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just look over to the next page and see. Would you cast your eyes over the next couple of paragraphs on the next page and see if there's any further comment specifically you want to make about that.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should probably quote -- take the quoted from -- mention the quote from the general, which would be General Praljak in this meeting, about three paragraphs down where he says: "Territorially speaking, we shall take what continues to be Croatian. What use is a territory while there are no Croats?"

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just hold on for a moment, please. The registry is going to the next page, I believe.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I'll continue. "We need the territory and the boarders that we inhabit. "The role the population plays on the stage is for political profit. This does not mean that it can play this role and succeed. "If the Croatian people don't want to move into and inhabit its own territory, then we have gained nothing." After a question, further down, from someone apparently representing Zenica, the response of General Praljak was: "The commission will continue its work and continue to make decisions."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just stop you there and just -- if you have any more comments about what you've just taken us to, otherwise I have a couple of other questions about the document and then subject to Judges' questions I'll move forward. If not, Mr. Tomljanovich, did -- in addition to Mr. Praljak, does the document indicate there was also some discussion involving Mr. Coric?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour. [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, just a brief intervention in order to save time for the sake of the cross. The last two documents referred to P 0178 [as interpreted], and the previous one 01788 deal with alleged statements by General Praljak at the meeting in Gornji Vakuf and the other meeting. We haven't seen that these are minutes from meetings. These are notes taken by someone, and we don't know who signed them, so we do not know on what basis this expert Witness claims that these are words spoken by General Praljak. These are notes made by someone, especially this latter document. The witness says it's the logbook of the operative zone, but I'm familiar with the logbook from the Kordic-Cerkez case and I don't think that's the document. I think this is the diary of General Blaskic, a completely different document. So they have been misrepresented. They have not been correctly described here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll put the question to the witness. Personally I'd like to go back to the beginning of the document. We see the date, the 2nd of April. It's a document that has been written on a notebook with squares, and someone wrote down what happened during a meeting of the brigade commanders in the zone. We can see on the document who are the brigade commanders present, the commanders of independent units, as well as assistant commanders, and then the drafter lists General Praljak, Kordic, Kostroman, Blaskic, and Coric. It is explained that the meeting begins and is chaired by General Praljak, beginning at 10.30 to finish at 12.00. And apparently the one who wrote these minutes recorded what he heard or what he summarised. Therefore, my question to you, Witness, is as follows: You have read what General Praljak stated during that meeting. Same question as my previous question. Does this -- of these -- statement of General Praljak in accordance with the Vance-Owen Plan, are they in line, these statements, with the meeting that took place and that was chaired by Mr. Prlic with Mate Boban and all the others? Do the statements of General Praljak find themselves in line with all of these other documents or have you noticed differences between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, again, this gets a little bit beyond the scope of this report. However, based not just on the material which I reviewed for this report but other material which will be introduced by other witnesses, I think General Praljak's statements are consistent with other statements we see in other documents from other witnesses, which I haven't cited in this report because I expect them to be addressed by another witness, and it's outside of the scope of what I was intending to do. But I do think they're in keeping with the general approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may. I do apologise for interrupting. But if the witness says that this was not within the scope of his report, why are we dealing with it now? This is just something mentioned in passing. "We found Praljak here, so let's bring Praljak in." We have an expert witness now. We have received the report, and we know what the scope of the report is. If other evidence is being slipped in by the way, we should have been informed about it. The witness is being made use of to say something he has not prepared to testify about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I take good note of your comments. I do not see in what way the statements of the witness can prejudice your client, but maybe I'm mistaken. Mr. Praljak, you want to take the floor, but first tell us why you want to speak, because we want to avoid any problems. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] With reference to what Mr. Tomljanovich has just read out, I do not deny the fact that at that time I attended that meeting. I only failed to understand what it was I was supposed to have said, because the sentences read out are sentences I don't understand. They've been translated again and again, and I don't recognise these words. I don't understand what it is I'm supposed to have said.
