utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown the map number 11 from Exhibit P 09276. And in particular, please, map number 11. I'm told it would be page 12 in e-court. Sir, using this map, looking at the -- which is -- the Chamber's previously seen, it's been discussed with other witnesses, the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, to your knowledge, sir, looking at approximately the middle of the map and locating the municipalities of Vares and Kakanj -- yes.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at this particular map showing the Vance-Owen provinces, and we were discussing earlier provinces 3, 8 and 10 which are shaded here in blue, if you look here in the middle near the number 9 where it's white, right under the number 9 there's Kakanj, and to the right of that is Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, sir, whether Vares and Kakanj as the Vance-Owen map evolved in 1993 up until the late spring and early summer of 1993, did that -- did provinces -- did the so-called Croat provinces, 8 and 10, ever include Kakanj or Vares?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I suspect at some point we're going to get some historical background from our historian here as to what was happening in those locations at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look at -- next at P 03796.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas, what kind of intervention has that been? Is that a question or an objection? I think that's the two things you are allowed to make at this stage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the gentleman is an expert. He's an historian. Now they're talking about documents of evacuation. Is this in the abstract? Is something happening at the time? Is there a reason why the gentleman spent seven and a half years -- I think it helps the Trial Chamber understand why this information is being brought forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, that's for the Prosecution. The Prosecution is leading their evidence and then afterwards you can challenge and ask what is left open and correct and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. This is a very unusual process. I've never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me just be very, very -- respond very briefly, Your Honours. The Court has the entire report and virtually everything that I've talked about yesterday and today is discussed in much greater detail in the report. The procedure that the Chamber has invited us to follow is to allow the expert to essentially hit, if you want to call it highlights, my friends on the other side might call it the lowlights, I don't know, but hit various aspects of the report and in -- in a summary overview sort of way. If the Chamber's concerned that I am already behind in my time, I can assure you we would be much further behind if we covered all these topics in full detail. Further, the Chamber has directed the Prosecution to go through those particular exhibits in the report which it seeks to have admitted into evidence. There again, all I can do at this point given the time limitations is try to put what I consider the most important exhibits before the Chamber and, necessarily so, there's a limited time to do that. The Chamber has seen over the last -- since yesterday and the Chamber has had a number of questions about the documents, good questions, reasonable questions. And if we had more time I myself would have spent more time on each document but if I do that we wouldn't get very far and unfortunately those are the rules that, in the circumstances that we -- all of us find ourselves in. If Mr. Karnavas wants to talk and use his time in cross-examination to go into the report, he has the whole report. He can go through any part of it that he would like to in great detail. So if I can again ask the witness to look at P 03796.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, sir, can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the 48th session of the HVO HZ HB, which were held on the 29th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And specifically to the topic at hand, the refugees or displaced persons, can I ask you please to look at -- to be shown page 4 of the document under item 14. And can you give us -- again, can you just look at item 14 in relation to your report.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Item 14 deals with some of these same issues. First thing to be underscored is paragraph 3, in which Mr. Zubak reports on the measures which were taken to anticipate the 10.000 or so Croats from Central Bosnia they expect to have come. After emphasising certain problems he talks -- he goes on. And then at the bottom, the very last paragraph, it states: "Bearing in mind the situation on the ground, and in particular the migration of the Muslim population, a unanimous decision was taken to expand the service for the exchange of prisoners and other persons to include representatives of the municipalities of Mostar, Capljina, Livno, and Stolac." And then it lists who their own members on this commission would be. I'm sorry, that's period, closed quote, and then they list the members they are appointing to this committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In addition to and again taking stepping aside from the current topic but because its in this particular document if I can ask you to look at the mention page, be shown the top of page 5 in reference to something you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- a couple of moments ago.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first paragraph there and this refers to what we were talking about earlier. I remembered correctly. What it says here is that "given the military situation, and particularly in the territory of Mostar, it was agreed that president Dr. J. Prlic should hold special working meetings with the collegiums of the Departments of Defence and the Interior."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What is whatever that word is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the B/C/S in front of me but I expect it would be "kolegij," and that would be a meeting of the department head or minister. In this case the department head still with all of his assistants. So it would be the head of the Department of Defence and all of his assistant department heads, as well as the head of the interior department and all of his head -- assistants with Mr. Prlic. So this would be a narrower meeting of people concerned with security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I next ask you, then, to look at Exhibit P 04282 [Realtime transcript read in error, "04218"].

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us what that document is, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document from Mr. Prlic to the Vares municipal government on the 18th of August, 1993. And this is in regard to the evacuation of Croats from Kakanj who had been living already as refugees in Vares. And he mentions that they will secure their evacuation to Western Herzegovina. One thing which needs to be underlined is that in the second paragraph here when he mentions that he's prepared for the -- or that they have prepared for the transport and they ask them to, and here's the quote, beginning mid sentence. But to save on time I'll start here, "... secure the consent of the 'S' side for transportation over territories that they control."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From your research, sir, can you tell us what the reference to "S" side or who the reference is to or what?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a great number of documents which we found in the Zagreb archives since the year 2000, coming from this area of Central Bosnia, in particular Kiseljak, and -- and that part of Central Bosnia, they refer to the Serbs as either "S" in quotation marks or, as the "XY" side in quotation marks. But given the number of documents we've seen, it's very clear that that's what they mean and that they use it consistently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And if -- sorry. Then if we can go then back to, I'm afraid, to the final document again at the end of the bundle. P 09551. And again, Mr. President, with my apology, this is again a document where the translations are currently in separate components and there is not a continuous page reference. In the B/C/S document, for those looking at that, or if it assists the registry at all, it is -- it can be found in the pages 0040-5261 through 0040-5264. And in the English version it's almost -- in fact, it's the last three pages of the English -- last three pages of the English translation. So if you just go back until you're almost in the B/C/S, you'll find the top of the page, says, "Department for Refugee Care." Thank you very much to the registry for your assistance on that. If I can ask you then to go to the next page of that document. Again, it's a bit different than the one I had. Can you scroll down, please. On to the next page. Sir, if I can direct your attention -- if you will refer to this because, at least those working in English will be referring to exactly the same format, the reference to the third paragraph starting on this page. Do you see references to 'a movement of Croats from Kakanj"?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the third paragraph. 10.500 Croats from Kakanj and Kraljeva Sutjeska to Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And after that paragraph, can you tell us, does it make reference to an evacuation from Vares later that year?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. In the next paragraph it mentions 2.986 persons, being the first huge evacuation from Vares and taking place on the 30th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where were these people located in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here to the municipalities of Capljina and Stolac, which is south of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And beyond that can you -- was there a second movement of population from Vares?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. The second huge wave of evacuations it says here took place on the 4th of November, 1993, and it says about 5.500 people expelled from Kakanj, and that 1.700 of them were directly accommodated, and I think in this sense "directly" means immediately, in the Republic of Croatia and the rest of them were accommodated in the municipalities of Livno, which is Western Bosnia, Ljubuski, Citluk, and Capljina, all in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If I might -- Mr. President, I've been -- indicate there is a problem on page -- of the transcript and unfortunately the page has gone by, I believe, but the last -- not this exhibit but the previous exhibit in the transcript apparently was referred to, I'm told, as P 04218. It may be that I misspoke. It should be P 04282. All right. Well, we'll start the next topic, I suppose, this evening and I want to turn to the question of the HVO prisons or camps. Did you look at that the structures and processes involved with the prison and camps operated by the HVO during 1993?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As part of your report did you research documents showing how various of the camps were established, how they were operated and closed -- and if they were closed at some point?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Not for all of the detention centres, but for some of them to show the general pattern, and to show how -- how the organs and structures of Herceg-Bosna dealt with that and who was responsible for what.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look now at P 00452. And can you tell us what that document is and how it relates to the part of your report dealing with the camps.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Or prisons.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the decision of the 3rd of September, 1992, signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic, establishing the central military prison for the HZ HB at the Heliodrom barracks near Mostar, and appointing the warden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The term "warden" seems to me surprising. Would it be the prison governor in normal English language? The terminology of the United Kingdom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's -- United Kingdom I'm not sure. I can only tell you what it might be in the Croatian, and I know that it often gets translated differently. I've seen both director and warden in translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the B/C/S version if that will assist. If we go to item number 2 on the B/C/S version, and as we have in the past would you just read that in the original language and --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. It says: [Interpretation] "2. For the warden of the central military prison. Mr. Mile Pusic, Krusevo, Mostar, is appointed."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Ravantlje" means "director," in literal translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we then go to Exhibit P 00515, the order by -- order by Mr. Stojic of the 3rd of September, 1992. Would you look at this document and tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, this is a continuation of the same activity, and this order is signed by Valentin Coric on the 22nd of September, 1992, and addressed to his assistant for investigations. Here it is translated as the governor of the central military prison and the governors, the four governors of HVO military remand prisons. And it's establishing -- it's also again ordering for a central military prison to be established at the barracks situated at the Mostar heliport or Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in this order does Mr. Coric indicate who will be responsible for executing, carrying out his order?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does. In the last paragraph in the order, if we could move down to the -- yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in this order, first of all, it says, "to establish a central military prison in the barracks situated at the Mostar heliport." Now, what I'm interested in is the second paragraph where I see that in this military prison there were prisoners of war, and then it says: "And army prisoners (both military and civilian)." What are your conclusions in that respect? I'm not asking about speculation here, I'm asking about your conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conclusion which is not based on any other documentation but my assumption that prisoners taken by the army would be civilian could mean males in service age or it could mean any other civilian prisoners that the -- that the army or military bring in. Which of that -- which it is, I don't know from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can -- if we can perhaps finish this -- next couple documents before 7.00. Look at Exhibit P 02679. Can you tell us about that document, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a decision signed by Jadranko Prlic on the 8th of June, 1993, to set up the county military prison and the county prison for the municipalities of Capljina, Neum, Ljubuski, and Ravno in Gabela.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And does it say when this decision goes into effect?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the decision takes into effect immediately and that it will be published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we next go to P 02674.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A question from me. This is a decision to set up a prison, Gabela, but it says the county military prison and the county prison. So was it a prison that was both a military prison and a civilian prison at the same time? Is that what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It may or may not assist in looking at the next document. If you have Exhibit P 02674 and tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the appointment on the same day, also signed by Jadranko Prlic, to appoint the head of the county military prison in Gabela.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boko Previsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now this particular decision, it does not reference the county prison but only the county military prison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I can show you finally for today Exhibit P 07668. You have that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a translation from the Official Gazette of a decision made by Jadranko Prlic -- or signed by Jadranko Prlic on the 22nd of December, 1993, and this nullifies the two orders of 8th of June, 1993, which we've seen before. This is undoing the foundation of the prison and the appointment of its director. And I should note that the -- this document was reprinted in the Official Gazettes, but I haven't been able to find the actual opening of the -- of Gabela or the appointment of its director in the Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Other than the documents that we looked at a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but those are from the Official Gazettes. Those are original copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The effect of the decision reflected on P 07668 is the Gabela prisons were closed.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that concludes our time for today. I can either catch up on the exhibits now. I suppose we can do it first thing in the morning, whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have a list of your exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. We will tender -- I'm told from previously I failed to tender P 01789, and then more recently P 00410, P 00511, P 09551, P 03052, P 03191, P 02283, P 03413, P 09276, if not previously admitted. We think it has been, but if it hasn't, I tender it now. P 03796, P 04282, P 00452, P 000515, P 02679, P 02674, and P 07668.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Just briefly. I stand by the objection I made with respect to document 03052. The document isn't signed. It hasn't got a date. There is no preamble. So what is the provenance? The witness said that it probably came from the archives of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but we know nothing for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another few seconds. Tomorrow, the Prosecution will have two hours to complete the examination-in-chief. As you know, the Defence teams in theory have tomorrow and the following day, and we said that you must decide how to divide the time up between you, and you'll have Monday as well, so you will three days in total. Now, at this stage, Mr. Karnavas, have you reached an agreement with your colleagues as to how to divide up the time, or do you want the Trial Chamber tomorrow at 2.15, before starting, to divide up the time for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I understand that you've already decided that for us. You gave us the amount of time, divided by six --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We haven't decided anything for us yet. We're waiting for you to tell us how you intend to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the sense that -- well, there are six of us, and among ourselves we know what we need to do. I've repeatedly objected to this process but you've told us this is the amount of time. We have about 12 hours or so among ourselves, perhaps 14. We divide it by six, and then if somebody wants to give up their time to another team because they won't use it, that's the way we'll proceed. Obviously, as I've said before, this is not in my opinion appropriate under the circumstances when you have somebody spending seven and a half years on a report, but we will live by the Court's decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I anticipate -- in fact we do now have an agreement between the Defence teams as to how the time will be allocated and I think we'll be in a position to announce that to the Trial Chamber at the close of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Fine. Mr. Murphy, you're telling us that you're going to reach an agreement and that's what we the Judges would prefer. We would prefer you to decide amongst yourselves rather than have to decide for you. Of course, you can always calculate by dividing by six, but perhaps that rule, divide it by six, isn't preferable. So I would prefer it if you were to divide up the time amongst yourselves between counsel and the accused to avoid any chaos or harbour the feeling that certain people weren't given the opportunity to raise the issues they wished to raise. So between now and then, you have time to meet and decide what you're going to do, reach an agreement. Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one second. I do appreciate the Chamber giving me the two hours tomorrow. Perhaps I was a bit grumpy before but we'll be able to complete given the extra time, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm quite confident it won't be necessary for the Court to make an allocation. The Defence counsel will be able to divide the time and in a manner that will be acceptable to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I apologise to the interpreters for taking 10 more minutes. We reconvene tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
